corrections: (1) NET CASH WRONG, THEN GOING STALE: the debate's ~$425M net cash (cash $1.52B vs debt $1.09B) misstates the primary filing — per the Q1-2026 release/10-Q (3/31/26) cash $1,504M + ST investments $13M vs total debt $568M ($33M ST + $535M LT term loan, covenants compliant) = NET CASH $949M, ~2.2x the debate's figure (the $1.09B 'debt' appears to have counted ~$524M of operating leases). BUT the 5/18/26 8-K then flips it forward: the board added $2B to the repurchase authorization (~$3.45B remaining as of 5/17/26), doubled the 2026 buyback target to $2B with the extra $1B to be executed WITHIN Q2, and is drawing $1B on the revolver for the buyback plus the pending Astreya acquisition — pro forma the net-cash buffer is roughly spent. The 'net-cash funds the buyback' framing becomes 'modestly levering to buy back ~10% of the company at ~7x earnings.' (2) SHARE COUNT: 474M outstanding / 477M diluted at 3/31/26, not ~490M; with $2B repurchased at ~$40-45 the exit-2026 count is ~440-450M — all per-share SoP values in the debate are understated ~3-8%. (3) FCF ANCHOR VERIFIES EXACTLY BUT IS FLATTERED: TTM FCF through Q1'26 = $2,470M (FY25 $2,665M = OCF $2,883M - capex $288M + $70M property sale; less Q1'25 $393M; plus Q1'26 $198M) — the debate's $2.47B is spot-on. However FY25 FCF was 120% of net income (working-capital assisted), Q1'26 FCF fell to $198M from $393M ($323M ex-property-sale), and FY26 GAAP FCF will absorb $230-320M of Project Leap charges — normalized FCF ~ net income puts the multiple nearer 8.5x than 7.4x. Cheapness survives normalization; the adverse ~$41 floor recomputes to ~$40 (8 x $2.27B updated TTM + $0.95B net cash on 474M) — but note the tape already traded through it ($37.08 52-wk low in June), so the 'floor is 2-3% below' claim was optimistic. (4) CATALYST CLAIMS STALE — IN THE THESIS'S FAVOR: risk_reward says 'the re-rating has no clock' and the debate said no forced-seller washout exists. Post-debate facts: (a) the 5/18/26 accelerated buyback (~5% of the float in one quarter) is a dated, hard capital-return event; (b) CTSH was DELETED from the Nasdaq-100 effective 6/22/26 — the mechanical index flush the debate said didn't exist actually happened, into the $37.08 low, and is now largely behind (stock $41.07 on 7/2/26, +6% on the day); (c) Q2 earnings 7/29/26 is the live test. (5) BEAR'S CONFIRMING INDICATOR CURRENTLY INVERTED: the bear names 'bookings weakening' as confirmation — Q1'26 bookings grew 21% (TTM $29.6B, +11%), 7 large deals, >70% large-deal TCV growth, and the FY26 adjusted-operating-margin guide was RAISED to 16.0-16.2%. The structural AI-deflation repricing is real and consensus-forming (Berenberg Buy->Hold, PT $81->$59, June 2026, citing faster-than-expected AI transition; Accenture tightened FY guidance June 2026; stock -53% from the $87.03 high), but as of the latest primary print it shows up nowhere in bookings, margin, or EPS guidance. (6) MISSED CONTINGENCIES, NOT DISQUALIFIERS: (a) India ITD dispute on the 2016 $2.8B CTS-India buyback — ITD asserts an additional Rs33B ($353M at 3/31/26 FX); $369M already on deposit with the ITD (carried as an asset); merits pending at the Madras High Court; ZERO reserves recorded; 2013 transaction ($523M) also in litigation with no specific demand — worst case is a several-hundred-$M cash hit, partly offset by the unrecorded ~$298M Syntel/TriZetto award in Cognizant's FAVOR (USDC-SDNY post-trial order 3/27/26, judgment entry pending, appeal expected). (b) TriZetto Provider Solutions data breach (intrusion from Nov 2024, discovered 10/2/25, ~3.4M individuals) drew multiple consumer class actions in NJ/MO in Dec 2025-Jan 2026; not listed as a material legal proceeding in the Q1'26 10-Q, but it sits on exactly the asset (TriZetto) that carries the SoP's premium healthcare multiple — a watch item. NET: every load-bearing number verifies against the primary filings, the errors found mostly UNDERSTATE the value case, and no disqualifier surfaced. The genuine unresolved risk is the terminal one the bear already owns: whether 7-8x FCF is the bottom of a fear-print or the top of a melt.
